title: What If the Black Sunday Dust Storm Hit Today?

scenes.text: What if the Black Sunday dust storm hit today? It blotted out the sun for hours.
On April 14, 1935, a wall of dust rolled across the Great Plains, hundreds of miles wide.
It stood thousands of feet high, and survivors said you couldn't see your hand in front of your face.
A cold front dropped the temperature more than 30 degrees in about two hours.
Birds, mice and jackrabbits fled ahead of it, and many didn't survive.
Estimates say 300,000 tons of topsoil were stripped away, and some of the dust reached the East Coast.
